name: ANSI three-state inverter with active-low enable
summary: Inverter triangle with an enable lead and bubble entering its side, driving a bus only when enabled.
description: The three-state inverter is a triangle with an output bubble and a control lead entering the sloping side. A bubble on the control lead means output enable is active low, which is the arrangement on many octal line drivers. When disabled, the output is high impedance.

On bus schematics these devices are usually drawn in groups of eight with a shared enable. Drafters should label the enable net once for the group and show which controller output drives it, so the reader can see when the bus is driven.
The symbol does not show bus hold, pull-up or pull-down arrangements needed to keep a disabled bus at a defined level. Those components must be drawn separately.
readingNotes: Check the bubble on the enable lead; it sets the enable polarity.
Look for bus-keeper or pull resistors on the driven net.
drawingChecklist: Draw the enable lead touching the sloping side of the triangle.
Show the shared enable source for a group of drivers.
distinction: The non-inverting three-state buffer has no output bubble.
